https://www.politico.eu/article/german-l.text: BERLIN —Senior conservative and social-democrat lawmakers in Germany’s governing coalition are urging the EU to sanction Israel’s Minister of National Security Itamar Ben-Gvir after he called for nightly targeted killings in Gaza. “I think targeted killings should be carried out in Gaza, remove 30, 40 [people] every night,” said Ben-Gvir, leader of the far-right Jewish Power party, in a podcast episode released last Saturday. “Not just those who pose an immediate threat. No, there are people there who are not worthy of life. They shouldn’t live. They’re not even people.” The comments drew an unusually sharp response from German Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s conservatives. Advertisement Advertisement “Ben-Gvir’s inhumane remarks can only be condemned,” Jürgen Hardt, foreign policy spokesperson for the Christian Democratic Union/Christian Social Union parliamentary group, told POLITICO. “The EU should sanction him as a sign of the universal validity of human dignity and human rights.” Hardt went further, saying he was convinced an Israeli government without Ben-Gvir or fellow far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich would bring Europe and Israel closer together. Germany’s Social Democrats struck a similar tone. Adis Ahmetović, the party’s foreign policy spokesperson, said the two ministers had shocked international opinion well before their latest statements, and urged the German government to support sanctions against both. The criticism extended across the political spectrum. The Left’s Dietmar Bartsch called Ben-Gvir’s remarks “deeply inhumane,” and urged Berlin and Brussels to consider sanctions, including an entry ban. Markus Frohnmaier, the far-right Alternative for Germany party’s foreign policy spokesperson, said calling for the indiscriminate killing of people who posed no immediate threat crossed “a clear line.” Green Member of Parliament Marlene Schönberger branded Ben-Gvir a “far-right extremist” and said his comments were “deeply inhumane,” adding that they had “nothing whatsoever” to do with Israel’s right to defend itself and its citizens. The statements mark a significant shift in Berlin. Germany has repeatedly pushed back against EU measures targeting Israel, including proposed sanctions on Ben-Gvir in June and, as recently as last month, restrictions on trade with illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank. Advertisement Advertisement EU sanctions require unanimity, giving Berlin considerable sway over whether the bloc can move. Merz’s government has not yet followed the lawmakers’ lead. The Foreign Ministry declined to take a position Monday, while some in government fear sanctioning Ben-Gvir just weeks before Israel’s Oct. 27 election could play into his hands. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul will meet his EU counterparts in Ireland on Sept. 1 and 2, where Ben-Gvir’s remarks and the war in Gaza are likely to loom over discussions. Maximilian Heimerzheim contributed to reporting. Ezt a törvényjavaslatot még nem nyújtották be, a jövő évi költségvetési tervezetben ugyanakkor még biztosan számolnak a volt köztársasági elnököknek járó egyik juttatási formával: a jótékonysági kerettel. Az idei évhez hasonlóan 2027-ben is fejenként 73 millió forintos állami keretből adakozhat civil szervezeteknek és alapítványoknak Schmitt Pál, Áder János, Novák Katalin és Sulyok Tamás. A hivatalban lévő köztársasági elnök, Baka András és az Országgyűlés elnöke, Forsthoffer Ágnes 100 millió forintos keretet kapott jótékonysági célra. A hivatalban lévő köztársasági elnök, az Országgyűlés elnöke és a volt államfők 2012 óta kapnak éves keretet a központi költségvetésből, hogy az általuk kiválasztott alapítványoknak és civil szervezeteknek adományozhassanak. A jogszabály szerint pályázat útján vagy egyedi döntés alapján dönthetnek a felajánlásokról, és mindössze egy korlátot vezetett be a törvény: nem lehet közcélú felajánlásban részesíteni pártot, pártnak anyagi támogatást nyújtó szervezetet, és közvetlen politikai tevékenységet folytató szervezetet. A péntek este benyújtott költségvetési tervezetből az is kiderült, hogy a Magyar-kormány jövőre is biztosítja több olyan intézetnek a működését, amit az Orbán-kormányok alapítottak. Ilyen például a magyarság eredetének, történetének és kultúrájának interdiszciplináris kutatására létrehozott Magyarságkutató Intézet, amely 2026-ban 1,04 milliárd forintot kapott a működésére az államtól. Jövőre ennél 13 millió forinttal több jut nekik. Az intézet főigazgatója korábban Kásler Miklós volt, most Lezsák Sándor volt fideszes országgyűlési képviselő lánya, M. Lezsák Gabriella. Szintén megmarad a 2012-ben a magyar örökség korszerű újrafogalmazása céljából alapított Nemzetstratégiai Kutatóintézet, de nekik közel 300 millió forinttal kevesebb állami támogatással kell beérniük. Így is valamivel több mint 1 milliárd forintból kutathatják jövőre a nemzet stratégiáját. Ugyancsak a második Orbán-kormány hozta létre a miniszterelnök irányítása alatt álló Nemzeti Örökség Intézetet, amely az idei közel 2,5 milliárdos állami forrás után csak valamivel több mint 2 milliárd forintra számíthat 2027-ben. Az Orbán-kormány 2018-ban döntött a család- és népesedéspolitikáját támogató Kopp Mária Intézet a Népesedésért és a Családokért (KINCS) nevű szervezet felállításáról, amely idén 985,4 millió forint állami forrásból kutathatott. https://www.dw.com/en/putin-proposes-sec.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PeoW Prefer DW on Google A Ukrainian soldier from an anti-drone unit patrols a street in Kostiantynivka (January 2026) Image: Diego Herrera Carcedo/Anadolu/picture alliance Advertisement Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a humanitarian mission in the city of Kostiantynivka similar to a recent operation in Oleshky . According to Putin, Russia has control of the city in the Donbas; the remaining civilian population, he says, could be evacuated. It would take five days to clear the access roads. The Russian leader has suggested that human rights organizations from Ukraine and Russia and delegates from the foreign press be incorporated into the mission. Putin's proposal comes after discussions between the Russian government and US representatives, who have been negotiating to try to bring an end to Russia's war against Ukraine . Experts say that while Russia is indicating a readiness to make agreements, at the same time it is propagating its own depiction of the situation on the front line. In July, Russia announced that it had taken Kostiantynivka but did not provide any proof. Ukraine says the fighting there is still ongoing. Experts from the Ukrainian open-source interactive map of military operations project DeepState say that the city is still controlled by the Ukrainian army, but that the situation there is "extremely difficult." Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy visited the main command post of a brigade defending Kostiantynivka in March 2026 Image: Ukrainian Presidential Press Service/AFP Responding to the proposal, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told journalists: "Putin simply wants us to leave Kostiantynivka so that they can move in and occupy the entire city." He emphasized that Ukraine had always given the civilian population in Kostiantynivka opportunities to leave, and said that Russia had used the temporary ceasefire in Oleshky to bring military equipment and weapons into the city. What is the situation for civilians? Kostiantynivka is the southernmost city in the so-called Donetsk "fortress belt," which also includes Druzhkivka, Kramatorsk and Sloviansk . Taking Kostiantynivka would open the way for Russian troops to advance to Druzhkivka, and on to the conurbation of Sloviansk and Kramatorsk. Oleksandr Kovalenko, a military expert at the Dmytro Tymchuk Center for Security Studies, a Ukrainian think tank, said Kostiantynivka's role is similar to that of Bakhmut, Avdiivka or Chasiv Yar — towns whose defensive installations were able to hold back Russian enemy forces for years. Local authorities say the humanitarian situation in the city, whose population before the start of Russia's full-scale invasion was around 70,000, is catastrophic and that some 340 civilians remain. They add that Kostiantynivka has no central water, electricity or gas supplies, there is no public transport, and since the spring of 2026 people have only been able to evacuate on foot. "Those who stayed in Kostiantynivka need to be evacuated, they need a chance of a better life," military analyst Denys Popovych told DW. However, he added that an evacuation was virtually impossible without a ceasefire, as Russian troops had occupied the road between the town and Druzhkivka and drones were being deployed throughout the region. Ukraine, therefore, could not carry out such an operation unilaterally. "It still takes two to tango — to evacuate the people, that is," he said. Humanitarian proposals as leverage Kovalenko believes that Moscow is simply using the humanitarian issue for purposes of manipulation and to strengthen its negotiating position. The Russian army, he said, wants to gain time in order to reinforce units fighting in the vicinity. Yevhen Zakharov, the director of the Kharkiv Human Rights Protection Group, has similar concerns. "I'm afraid that this proposal by the Russians has very different objectives to those they claim to pursue," he told DW. He described Putin's initiative as suspect, and said the Ukrainian side should treat it with the utmost caution. The aftermath of a Russian attack on a residential building in Kostiantynivka in November 2024 Image: Ukrinform/dpa/picture alliance Kyiv is in a difficult position, as the idea of a mission for Kostiantynivka is also being pushed by US intermediaries. "If we reject it, they'll say to us: 'You're rejecting peace proposals, you're not taking care of your own citizens, why should we keep talking to you, Zelenskyy wants to continue the war.' This is precisely the calculation behind it all," said Popovych. Ceasefire as military tactic After the end of the ceasefire in Oleshky , which was in place from October 27 to November 1, the Ukrainian General Staff announced that, in that time, the Russians had rotated their troops, entrenched their positions, reinforced measures to repel drones and brought in ammunition. Kovalenko is convinced that the reason Russia is proposing a ceasefire is because its army is gradually losing ground in Kostiantynivka. From Moscow's perspective, the Russian troops that are meant to be storming the city are in urgent need of reinforcements, which they can't get because of the fighting on the ground. "If a so-called humanitarian mission were to take place in Kostiantynivka, it would be a disaster for Kyiv, because Russia would use that time to consolidate forces that would enable it to take the city," he warned. Apartment buildings and a church in Kostiantynivka were damaged in Russian attacks in December 2025 Image: National Police of Ukraine/AFP How should Kyiv respond to Moscow's proposal? Popovych, however, does not think Ukraine should reject the Russian proposal. In his view, Kyiv should base its tactics on experiences with previous ceasefires and insist on very clear conditions in advance. "If there is a ceasefire, soldiers currently at their posts should stay there and not move," he suggested. Oleksandr Pavlichenko from the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union believes Ukraine should submit a counter-proposal, which envisages the withdrawal of Russian troops from the Ukrainian city and the unimpeded departure of the civilian population. The human rights activist said that, for a genuine humanitarian mission to be put in place, a strong, neutral third party should be brought in to supervise and ensure safe passage. In his view, the only party with such a mandate is the International Committee of the Red Cross. "If a proposal comes from only one side, and from a side such as Russia, it doesn't inspire confidence," he said. This article was originally written in Ukrainian.
